compositions.title: Seed and water
compositions.text: Se mann hæfde sǣd and wæter. Ðā męnn hæfdon hof and fuglas. Ðā fuglas lifdon on hiera hofe. Se mann sealde ðǣm mannum sǣd and wæter. Hīe lufodon ðā fuglas and hīerdon hīe. Hīe sealdon him sǣd and wæter. Hīe ne sęndon ðā fuglas. Hīe gefręmedon hiera weorc and geręston hīe. Se mann sægde: “Ic lufie ðā fuglas.”
compositions.intended_meaning: The man had seed and water. The men had a dwelling and birds. The birds lived in their dwelling. The man gave the men seed and water. They loved the birds and heard them. They gave them seed and water. They did not send the birds. They performed/completed their work and rested. The man said: “I love the birds.”
compositions.reference_note: The intended narrative has the men receive seed/water and pass it to the birds. Plural hīe and dative him do not by themselves distinguish those antecedents. The task must permit a contextually defensible alternative or state the intended recipient; it must not present spelling as proof of a unique reference. All Ðā/ðā here are article forms, not the temporal adverb.
compositions.auditor_precheck: Grammar auditor checked ordinary valencies and selected hīe; coordinator corrected mannum against actual Unit1 paradigm. Exact direct quotation applies U02-DIRECT-SPEECH to the fully taught past reporting form. Final token checks pending.
compositions.validation: Every token matched exact selected prior/new form and intended case/person cell.

compositions.title: The workers and the birds
compositions.setting: Four workers, A, B, C and D, are together with the birds. Speaker labels identify the addressees. In the last turn, wē includes all four workers and gē addresses B, C and D.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Ic hæbbe sǣd. Ðū hæfst wæter.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Wit sęllað ðǣm fuglum męte. Hīe hīerað unc.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Git lufiað ðā fuglas. Ic hīere inc.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Wē lufiað hīe. Gē hīerað hīe, and hīe hīerað ēow.

compositions.text: Ic hæbbe sǣd. Ðū hæfst wæter. Wit sęllað ðǣm fuglum męte. Hīe hīerað unc. Git lufiað ðā fuglas. Ic hīere inc. Wē lufiað hīe. Gē hīerað hīe, and hīe hīerað ēow.
compositions.intended_meaning: A: I have seed. You have water. B: We two give the birds food. They hear us two. C: You two love the birds. I hear you two. A: We love them. You hear them, and they hear you.
compositions.reference_note: The English speaker labels are framing, not Old English vocabulary or an untaught speech construction. The fourth participant makes the final plural reference unambiguous without falsely claiming plural pronouns cannot refer to two.

teaching_examples.purpose: Nominative personal subject, independently inflected weak verb, accusative noun object.
Pronoun object retains accusative; its plural number does not control the singular verb.
Dative recipient and accusative thing with an independently formed present of sęllan.

teaching_examples.text: Hiera fuglas libbað on his hofe.
teaching_examples.meaning: Their birds live in his dwelling.
teaching_examples.purpose: Invariant plural and masculine-singular possessors; possessed noun governs agreement and external case.
Accusative feminine personal pronoun used reflexively; the ordinary spelling is not a special reflexive form.

teaching_examples.meaning: You two do not hear the man.
teaching_examples.purpose: Dual subject takes plural verb; ne precedes the finite verb in this simple clause.
Bounded direct quotation, not an indirect clause or infinitive complement.
Class II preterite; the masculine accusative article identifies the object.
